flow.zh: 美的時光是追憶的時光

zh: 干樂週轉的旋律戞然停住
en: Luodong's night is mild and easy
Shangri-La Farm
An air of anticipation fills everything
When the frogs' cry rises from beside the stream
The revolving melody of joy stops abruptly
The sky lanterns are lit one by one
Every sky lantern is tied to
The sound of wind, the sound of rain, the sound of reading aloud
Every sky lantern is charged with
Family matters, state matters, matters of the world
Every sky lantern carries its worry
Feelings for homeland, family, and friendship

zh: 天上諸神彷彿都齊聲歡唱：
en: It seems as if all the gods in heaven sing together in joy:
Come up! Come up!
All the care
All the blessings
All the hopes
And so
Sky lanterns rise, one after another
Scattering into the deep, distant beyond
As if starlight's long rays

zh: 明滅於柔靜的羅東夜晚
en: perhaps,
After long years have passed
Another sky of stars falls silent
A night of flickering fireflies
I will suddenly remember, for no reason
Those sky lanterns
Still lit
Still scattering in flight
Even the lone streetlamp beside the field
Also holding fast to that stretch of scenery
Revealing a faint blessing
With dim yellow light and shadow
Veiling the days of long ago
A melody of beauty, swaying
Just like a sky lantern drifting away
Tied to a dream
About to speak, yet unspoken
Flickering in the soft, quiet night of Luodong

points.zh: 天燈又稱孔明燈，相傳爲三國時期諸葛亮所創。諸葛亮當時被司馬懿困於平陽，製紙燈繫上求救信息，趁風勢放上天空，援軍得訉趕來，終得以脱險。天燈起初是爲了傳遞信息之用，經年演變而有節慶祈福許願的意涵。

每年元宵節，台灣北部最具有民俗色彩的文化活動，平溪放天燈，也具有傳遞信息的歷史典故。清朝道光年間，先民由福建惠安，安溪等地移入基隆河上游，十分寮一帶 (即平溪地區 )。村民辛勤開墾，村落富足。當時因山區偏遠，官府鞭長莫及，遂成爲山賊土匪出没之地。村民爲了保命逃生，每年冬至過後，村民便收拾細軟逃入深山避難，直到元宵前後，才派壯丁下山察看，確定安全無虞後，再放天燈報平安回村。此後十分寮村民便以放天燈来慶祝元宵節，并向鄰村互報平安。因此該地村民又稱天燈爲 " 平安燈 " 或 " 祈福燈 "  。一個默默無聞的偏遠小村，承襲了此一民俗文化的衣缽，延綿一两百年，如此源遠流長，竟然成爲馳名台灣的重要元宵節慶典儀式，更曾獲得Discovery票選爲世界十大夜間節慶嘉年華會之一。歷年來都吸引十多萬民衆前來参加， 而有「北天燈，南蜂炮」 (鹽水蜂炮) 的美譽。天燈燃起，希望再起，藉由天燈祈求許願，淨化心靈，編織夢想，留下美的經驗和記憶。胡爾泰有「平溪天燈」一詩：「 九色天燈飛夜空,  萬千宿願上蒼穹，繁星殞落平溪外，殘念猶存心宇中  」。
其實天燈的閩南口語和「添丁」相似，早期先民開墾需要勞力，加上農業社會重男輕女的觀念，男丁是勞力和生產力的代名詞。所以都會在廟宇祈福放天燈，天燈上常寫上「早生貴子」，「五穀豐收」之類的祈褔吉祥語。而元宵節是春耕季節的開始，先民藉由施放天燈，向祖先報平安，並向上天求庇佑，祈禱一年的希望。
points.en:
Every year at the Lantern Festival, the release of sky lanterns at Pingxi is the folk cultural event with the richest local color in northern Taiwan, and it also carries a historical significance as a means of transmitting messages. During the Daoguang era of the Qing dynasty, early settlers moved from Hui'an, Anxi, and other places in Fujian into the upper reaches of the Keelung River, into the Shifenliao area (present-day Pingxi district). The villagers worked hard to cultivate the land, and the village prospered. Because the mountainous area was remote and beyond easy reach of the authorities, it became a haunt for bandits and outlaws. To save their lives, every year after the winter solstice the villagers would pack up their belongings and flee into the deep mountains for safety, only returning around the Lantern Festival, when able-bodied men would first go down the mountain to check whether it was safe, and once safety was confirmed, release sky lanterns to signal "all is well" and call the villagers back. From then on, the villagers of Shifenliao used the release of sky lanterns to celebrate the Lantern Festival, and to signal to neighboring villages that all was safe. Because of this the villagers there also call the sky lanterns "peace lanterns" or "blessing lanterns." An obscure, remote little village inherited this folk cultural tradition, which has continued unbroken for one or two hundred years, and has now become a major Lantern Festival celebration famous throughout Taiwan, even once voted by Discovery Channel as one of the world's top ten night festivals. Over the years it has drawn more than a hundred thousand visitors, earning the reputation of "sky lanterns in the north, bee fireworks in the south" (referring to the Yanshui Beehive Fireworks Festival). As the sky lanterns rise, so does hope rise again; through the sky lanterns people pray and make wishes, purify their hearts, weave dreams, and leave behind beautiful memories and experiences. Hu Erh-tai wrote a poem, 'Pingxi Sky Lanterns': "Nine-colored sky lanterns fly into the night sky, carrying ten thousand wishes up to the heavens; as stars fall beyond Pingxi, lingering hopes still remain within the heart."
In fact, the Hokkien pronunciation of "sky lantern" resembles that of "adding a son." In earlier times, settlers needed labor for land reclamation, and combined with the traditional agrarian society's preference for sons over daughters, a male child was seen as synonymous with labor and productivity. So people would pray at temples and release sky lanterns for blessings, often writing auspicious wishes on the lanterns such as "may a noble son be born soon" or "may the five grains bring a bountiful harvest." And since the Lantern Festival marks the beginning of the spring planting season, the early settlers released sky lanterns to report safety to their ancestors, and to pray to heaven for blessing and protection, hoping for the fulfillment of the year's wishes.

points.zh: 祈福的天燈，除了民俗文化，感性的意義之外，背後還有精準的科學原理。天燈之所以會浮升，是依據浮力原理，就是「阿基米德浮力原理」，指的是 「物體在液體中所受到的浮力和它所排出的液重相等，而决定沉或浮的関键，則在密度。物體的密度比液體大的就下沉，密度小的就上浮。」天燈上升的主角是氣體。在尚未加熱前，天燈内外的大氣完全一樣，加熱之後，天燈裡的空氣受熱膨脹，很快的天燈就裝不下那麼多膨脹的空氣分子，多餘的空氣分子就溢出天燈之外，質量因而減少。密度等於質量除以體積，體積不變，質量减少，天燈裡的空氣密度便跟著變小，天燈也就冉冉浮升。載人的熱氣球也是同樣的原理。飛向天際的天燈，直到底部煤油紙燒完，才會自動下降。當成群的天燈齊放，紛紛騰空飛起，的確令人目不暇給。天燈隨風飛昇遠去，就像一顆顆帶火光的磒石凌越夜空，最後，天燈幻化成點點星光，遂漸消失於深邃暗夜。
points.en: Behind the sky lantern's blessing — beyond its folk-cultural and emotional significance — lies a precise scientific principle. The reason a sky lantern rises is based on the principle of buoyancy, namely "Archimedes' principle of buoyancy," which states that "the buoyant force an object experiences in a fluid equals the weight of the fluid it displaces, and whether it sinks or floats depends on density: an object denser than the fluid sinks, while one less dense floats." The main actor in the sky lantern's rise is gas. Before being heated, the air inside and outside the lantern is identical; once heated, the air inside the lantern expands, and soon the lantern can no longer contain all the expanding air molecules, so the excess air escapes from the lantern, reducing its mass. Since density equals mass divided by volume, and the volume stays the same while the mass decreases, the density of the air inside the lantern decreases, and the lantern gently rises. A hot-air balloon carrying passengers works on the same principle. A lantern flying toward the sky will only begin to descend once the kerosene-soaked paper at its base has burned out. When a whole cluster of sky lanterns is released together, rising one after another into the sky, it is truly a dazzling sight to behold. As the lanterns drift away on the wind, they look like meteors trailing fire crossing the night sky, and finally the lanterns dissolve into points of starlight, gradually vanishing into the deep night.
